evidence: The film structure was studied by means of a Philips MPD 1880 powder X-ray diffractometer using Cu K a radiation and Bragg–Brentano geometry, or with a Bruker D8 Advance X-ray diffractometer in grazing incidence mode (incidence angle 1/C176). The film thicknesses were evaluated by X-ray reflection measurements carried out using Bruker D8 Advance X-ray diffractometer in reﬂectance mode. To reveal possible composition gradients at oxide–electrode and oxide–oxide boundary areas and to estimate the thickness of oxide layer, the high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) was employed for selected samples using an electron microscope with field-emission gun TECNAI F30 ST operating at 300 kV. Dielectric properties of the films were measured after e-beam evaporation of shadow masked aluminum electrodes with the area of 0.204 mm 2 and thickness not lower than 100 nm, creating an array of metal–insulator–metal (MIM) type Mo/nanolaminate/Al capacitors. Capacitance–voltage curves were recorded using a HP4284A precision LCR-meter in a two-element series circuit mode. The stair-sweep voltage step was 0.05 V. The period between voltage steps was 0.5 s. The AC voltage applied to the capacitor was 0.05 V while the frequency of the AC signal could be varied between 100 kHz and 1 MHz. The current–voltage curves were measured with a Keithley 2400 Source Meter in the stair-sweep voltage mode while the voltage step used was 0.02–0.05 V. All measurements were carried out at room temperature.
